policy.purpose: Conceptual reference for translators and language reviewers. Definitions explain product meaning; they do not prescribe one translation for every locale or become runtime interface strings.
policy.userTerminology: Explicit user terminology choices and existing personal translation overrides take priority over built-in wording. Preserve those preferences consistently while retaining distinctions between concepts.
policy.context: Translate by semantic role and screen context, never by isolated dictionary substitution. Consult source anchors when a label is ambiguous. Product names, user data and code identifiers are not ordinary translatable prose.
policy.consistency: Use a consistent term for the same concept within one translation package. Related concepts may share roots, but Agent, Worker, Server, Project, Workspace and Conversation must remain distinguishable.
policy.technicalLiterals: Preserve exact commands, flags, URLs, paths, environment-variable names, JSON property names, serialized enum values, provider/model IDs and credential values. Translate display labels around them; a translated label must never become a control-flow identifier.
policy.arguments: Preserve named argument identifiers and their complete set in every plural form. Arguments may move naturally; the runtime inserts their values as data. Use argumentDescriptions and examples to determine meaning, not to replace actual runtime values.
policy.grammar: Use target-locale plural categories, natural word order, established software terminology and appropriate agreement. Do not mechanically preserve English capitalization or concatenate fragments that need inflection.
policy.sharedData: Do not translate stored user names, Prompt content, conversations, arbitrary errors or model-authored explanations as part of the UI catalog. Shared server data must not be rewritten into one viewer language.
policy.ambiguity: When semantic context is insufficient, flag the ambiguity for review. Do not invent a product capability or silently equate technical concepts.
policy.scope: Global describes resource scope within the deployment; it does not imply public Internet visibility or unrestricted permissions.

gromozeka.definition: The name of this AI assistant product, comprising Compose clients, a central Server, and execution Workers.
gromozeka.translationGuidance: Preserve the product name unless the user explicitly chooses a personal rendering. Do not translate it as an ordinary noun.

agent.definition: A server-managed AI participant and reusable configuration of model selection, ordered prompts, tools, skills and behavior. It can participate in a Conversation.
agent.translationGuidance: Use one consistent target-language term for the AI participant/configuration. It does not mean a human representative or an execution machine.

worker.definition: A named trusted execution process on a particular machine or device. It advertises capabilities and executes operations assigned to that exact Worker.
worker.translationGuidance: Keep the distinction from Agent and Server. A translation may use an established software term; do not imply a human laborer or automatic reassignment to another machine.

server.definition: The central service that manages users, catalogs, Conversations, turn orchestration, memory pipelines and routing to execution targets.
server.translationGuidance: Use the software/network meaning. It is a distinct execution target and is not a Worker.

client.definition: The user-facing Gromozeka application that connects to the Server, such as a desktop, browser or mobile Compose client.
client.translationGuidance: Use the software-application meaning, not a customer buying services.

project.definition: A logical working context that groups relevant resources and controls project membership. Conversations belong to Projects.
project.translationGuidance: Do not reduce this to a filesystem folder or Git repository. Global catalog objects can be shared across Projects in one deployment.

conversation.definition: A Project-owned exchange of messages with an explicit set of connected User and Agent participants. It is not bound to one Workspace.
conversation.translationGuidance: Use the established chat/conversation concept consistently. A Conversation may involve more than one participant or Agent.

workspace.definition: A logical Project resource; the currently implemented kind is a filesystem tree.
workspace.translationGuidance: Use a software working-area or workspace term. It is distinct from the Project that owns it and from its path on a specific Worker.

workspace_mount.definition: The binding recording that one particular Worker can access one Workspace at a Worker-local root path. Filesystem, shell and Git operations target this binding.
workspace_mount.translationGuidance: Mount has a filesystem-binding meaning. Preserve the combination of Worker, Workspace and local path; do not translate it as a physical mount or equate it with the Workspace itself.

runtime.definition: Depending on the label, the executing Gromozeka system/deployment or its active server-managed configuration. A runtime catalog configures live application behavior.
runtime.translationGuidance: In these settings it does not mean elapsed execution duration. Translate compounds from context: runtime catalog, runtime purpose and runtime overrides have different roles.
distinguishFrom: downloaded language runtime such as a JRE

runtime_assignment.definition: A configured selection of one model configuration for a Gromozeka workflow purpose such as normal chat, memory recall, or speech recognition. Optional stages can inherit a parent workflow selection.
runtime_assignment.translationGuidance: Assignment means assigning a model to a system function, not a homework task, a job ticket or a Worker placement.

runtime_purpose.definition: The named application workflow or stage for which a model is selected, for example Memory read / Planner or Text-to-speech.
runtime_purpose.translationGuidance: Render purpose as a role/function of a model call. A stage override changes the selected model for that stage.

turn.definition: One Agent response cycle in a Conversation. It may contain several model steps, tool calls/results and continuations before the final answer or termination.
turn.translationGuidance: Use a dialogue-cycle term. It is broader than a single model request or a single visible message; it is not physical rotation.

model_call.definition: One request to an AI provider/model and its resulting response. Multiple model calls may occur during a single Agent turn.
model_call.translationGuidance: Call means an API/model invocation, not a telephone conversation. Usage statistics count these calls.

tool.definition: A defined callable operation available to the AI system, with a stable contract/name and arguments, such as inspecting files, searching or controlling a browser.
tool.translationGuidance: Use the AI/software capability meaning. Tool identifiers remain literal even when surrounding UI labels are translated.

tool_call.definition: An invocation of one tool with arguments, followed by a tool result. The operation may run on the Server, a specific Worker or an external tool service according to its contract.
tool_call.translationGuidance: Call means invoking an operation. Keep call and result distinct. Do not imply that a requested action has already completed.

parallel_tool_calls.definition: Multiple tool invocations that may be issued or executed concurrently rather than strictly one after another. The exact UI setting determines whether it controls model permission or actual scheduling.
parallel_tool_calls.translationGuidance: Parallel refers to concurrency, not geometry, duplicate actions or multiple Agents. Do not claim concurrent execution when a control only permits the model to request several calls. This is a general concurrency term, not evidence that the current runtime executes every requested tool concurrently.

response_branch.definition: A mutually exclusive variant of a structured model-response protocol, such as tool_calls versus final_answer.
response_branch.translationGuidance: Branch here is a protocol/control-flow alternative, not a Git branch, a department, or necessarily a forked Conversation. Preserve exact discriminator values in code or technical examples.

prompt.definition: A stored instruction or context document, usually Markdown, included in an ordered stack that shapes an Agent behavior. Prompt content is user/server-managed data.
prompt.translationGuidance: Use the AI-instruction meaning here, not a popup dialog, a command prompt, a short UI hint or the adjective meaning quick. Translate editor labels, never the stored prompt text as part of UI localization.

skill.definition: A project-scoped imported Agent Skill package containing instructions and possibly related files/resources. Agents can discover and load it when needed.
skill.translationGuidance: Use a reusable AI capability/package meaning. Do not imply human proficiency or that enabling a Skill installs software, grants permissions, or automatically executes its files.

materialization.definition: Making a Skill package available as actual files in a Workspace on a Worker, according to its materialization policy and available mount.
materialization.translationGuidance: Use a concrete file-preparation/extraction meaning. It is different from loading instructions into model context and from running or installing the package. Avoid mystical or abstract realization language.

load.definition: In a UI action, read data into the application; for always-loaded tools or Skills, make definitions or instructions available in model context.
load.translationGuidance: Choose wording from the object being loaded. It does not mean CPU utilization, physical cargo, installing software or executing a script.

scope.definition: The ownership/availability boundary of a resource. In catalogs, Global applies across Projects in one deployment, while Project scope belongs to one Project. Memory scope further qualifies when information applies.
scope.translationGuidance: Use a contextual reach/ownership term. Global does not mean published on the Internet or accessible without authorization. Do not confuse scope with visibility of an open UI panel.

model.definition: An AI model selected from a provider; the UI may show a user-named model configuration that references the provider model identifier.
model.translationGuidance: Distinguish model weights/service identity from a configured model entry and from its connection. Preserve actual model IDs and user-given display names.

model_configuration.definition: A reusable catalog entry combining a connection, a provider model ID, display name and default generation/reasoning parameters.
model_configuration.translationGuidance: Translate the configurable-entry meaning. Two configurations may point to the same provider model with different parameters or connections.

model_spec.definition: Catalog metadata describing the capabilities and limits of a provider model, such as input modalities, context window and supported reasoning controls.
model_spec.translationGuidance: Spec means specification/capability description, not a configuration chosen by a user or an implementation detail to invent.

connection.definition: A configured provider-access route with its kind, credentials or CLI authentication, and exact execution target. Model configurations reference it.
connection.translationGuidance: Connection is a catalog configuration here, not merely a currently open network socket or a connectivity indicator. Do not imply automatic fallback to another provider or machine.

execution_target.definition: The exact place where a configured AI or tool operation executes: the Server or one named Worker, according to the operation.
execution_target.translationGuidance: Target means destination/executor, not a goal, target value or attack target. Preserve the promise of exact routing and no silent machine fallback.

reasoning.definition: The model reasoning/thinking behavior and provider-supported controls for it. Display settings affect reasoning information exposed by the model/provider.
reasoning.translationGuidance: Use the AI deliberation/thinking meaning, not a legal justification or a stored reason field. Do not imply access to hidden internal reasoning that the provider does not expose.

reasoning_effort.definition: A provider/model-supported qualitative level controlling reasoning, such as Low, Medium, High, Extra high or Max.
reasoning_effort.translationGuidance: Effort is an AI control level, not CPU load, a number of Agents, an output length or a fixed time allowance. Preserve distinctions between levels.

token.definition: A unit of text representation processed or generated by an AI model, used for context limits and usage counts. It is not necessarily one word or one character.
token.translationGuidance: Use the established AI-token term consistently. Token counts are numeric quantities and pluralize according to the target locale.

credential_token.definition: A secret credential used to authorize access to an account or browser extension, for example a per-user GitHub token or Browser Bridge extension token.
credential_token.translationGuidance: Use the security-credential meaning. Do not confuse it with model text tokens, quota units or a coupon; never modify an actual credential value.

quota.definition: A provider subscription usage allowance or capacity limit. Background pacing protects some capacity for foreground requests.
quota.translationGuidance: Keep quota distinct from money spent, per-call token limits and context-window capacity. Reserve and headroom refer to remaining allowance, not physical storage.

context_window.definition: The model limit for the context/tokens it can consider in a request, according to its specification.
context_window.translationGuidance: Window is an AI-capacity concept, not a visible application window or a time interval.

compaction.definition: Summarizing or condensing conversation context to fit model limits while preserving relevant information. A configured threshold determines when it may occur.
compaction.translationGuidance: Use a context-condensation meaning, not disk defragmentation, file compression, deleting the whole Conversation or forcibly squeezing objects.

memory.definition: Persistent semantic information the assistant can store, retrieve and maintain, including sources, claims, notes and action items within controlled banks/namespaces.
memory.translationGuidance: Use the assistant knowledge/remembering meaning. It is distinct from RAM, a context window and raw chat history; do not promise perfect factual truth.

memory_bank.definition: The trusted storage and access boundary for a set of memory records, such as a Project bank or a personal User bank.
memory_bank.translationGuidance: Use an organized store/boundary meaning. This is not a financial bank, a physical memory module or a model-selectable arbitrary global area.

memory_claim.definition: An atomic structured assertion about an entity, carrying subject, predicate, object/value, scope, status, validity and supporting evidence. It may be tentative, superseded or retracted.
memory_claim.translationGuidance: Use a factual-assertion meaning. A claim is not automatically proven true, a complaint, a demand, a legal claim or an insurance claim.

memory_note.definition: A reusable semantic memory fragment containing decisions, rationale, plans, hypotheses, lessons or context that need not be atomic factual assertions.
memory_note.translationGuidance: Use a stored note/knowledge-fragment meaning. Keep it distinct from a claim and an operational action item.

action_item.definition: A remembered operational commitment or follow-up with lifecycle, priority, blockers, acceptance criteria and closure state.
action_item.translationGuidance: Use a task/follow-up meaning; it is not a low-level tool action or merely a bullet point in text.

memory_source.definition: Original input material such as chat turns, tool outputs or imported documents, retained to support audit and repair of derived memory.
memory_source.translationGuidance: Use the evidentiary origin meaning. Source is not necessarily source code, and a derived summary must not be represented as the original quotation.

entity.definition: An identifiable person, organization, project, object or other subject referenced in structured memory. Canonicalization links references to a consistent identity.
entity.translationGuidance: Use the data/knowledge-model sense, not a supernatural being. Entity identity is distinct from the assertions stored about it.

embeddings.definition: Numeric vector representations of content used for semantic retrieval. Dimensions are the number of components in each vector.
embeddings.translationGuidance: Use established AI/vector terminology. Embedding is not inserting a webpage, physically embedding an object or adding a visible UI component.

recall.definition: Retrieving relevant stored memory before or during an Agent response. It may include planning a search and selecting useful candidates.
recall.translationGuidance: Use remembering/retrieval, not product recall, revoking a credential or recalling an employee from leave.

inheritance.definition: An optional setting may use its parent model/workflow value; an override replaces that value only for the named Agent or stage.
inheritance.translationGuidance: Use configuration inheritance, not genetic inheritance. Default often means no explicit override, not necessarily a fixed English-named model.
